description:
CSUTLDTC, the called date-validation subprogram, invoked as the @Service it became. LS-DATE='2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT='          ' are this case's two LINKAGE SECTION parameters (L84-L85); LS-RESULT PIC X(80) (L86) is the output and is asserted below as the single WS_MESSAGE_80 line. This program opens no file and is reached by no JCL, so it seeds no dataset, writes no record and takes no job parameter - its entire observable behaviour is the 80 bytes L97 moves into LS-RESULT and the severity L98 moves into RETURN-CODE. Expected values are STATICALLY DERIVED from the 01 WS-MESSAGE declaration at L42-L57 and the group move at L122, never captured from a COBOL run, which is impossible here. Arm 2 of the EVALUATE TRUE at L128-L149: FC-INSUFFICIENT-DATA, 88-level VALUE X'000309CB59C3C5C5' (L63), whose two leading halfwords are decoded rather than assumed - SEVERITY (L72) is 0x0003 = 3 and MSG-NO (L73) is 0x09CB = 2507 - so offset 0 carries '0003', offset 15 carries '2507' and RETURN-CODE is 3. The mask is ten blanks, and every one of those positions is a literal delimiter, so the picture string is WELL FORMED and this is not the 2518 that a malformed one reports: it simply declares no year, no month and no day, and IBM's documented minimum is a year with a month and a day, or a year with a day of the year, which is exactly what 2507 reports. Three spans repay reading against the source. WS-RESULT at offset 20 is the L132 literal 'Insufficient' moved into PIC X(15), so three of the four spaces that follow it are that pad and the fourth is the FILLER at L50. WS-DATE at offset 45 is NOT the date that was passed in: L105 moves the DECLARED length of LS-DATE - always 10, never the length of the text - into Vstring-length, L107-L108 place the date in both Vstring-text and WS-DATE, and L122 then moves the whole of WS-DATE-TO-TEST back over it, so the ten surviving bytes are the halfword 0x00 0x0A followed by only the first eight characters, '2022-07-'. That truncation is a defect of the source and is reproduced rather than repaired. WS-DATE-FMT at offset 66 is clean by contrast: L111-L113 fill it before the CALL at L116 and L122 targets WS-DATE alone, so the mask is echoed back verbatim - here as its full ten blanks, which is why the line closes with fourteen consecutive spaces once the FILLERs at L56 and L57 follow it. Against case01, which passes this same date with 'YYYY-MM-DD' and converts, the mask is isolated as the sole cause of the failure; against case06, which reaches this arm with 'YYYY      ', the guard is shown to fire for a mask that declares nothing at all as well as for one that declares only a year; and against case15, whose 'QQQQ-MM-DD' is rejected as a bad picture string, a well-formed but under-specified picture is separated from a malformed one.

THE TWO CALL PARAMETERS, DECLARED RATHER THAN SELECTED IN JAVA. unitStimulus.linkage carries this case's whole input: LS-DATE = '2022-07-19' and LS-DATE-FORMAT = '          ', each written out to the ten characters PIC X(10) declares at app/cbl/CSUTLDTC.cbl:84-85 with every trailing space visible - a mask longer than ten characters is TRUNCATED by the receiving field, and the truncation changes the message number, so the width has to be readable at the point the value is written. CSUTLDTC seeds no dataset and drives no screen, so these two values are the only thing a case varies; they used to live in a table in CSUTLDTCParityTest keyed by 'case01'..'case20', which meant this file stated an eighty-byte result with nothing in it to say what was validated, and cases that differ only in their input were indistinguishable on disk.
